note: The A tier and the B tier of one family share this contract, so their goldens and case generators stay interchangeable.
output: logits of shape (B, num_classes); this is a whole classifier, not an attention core
stages: 4 stages with patch merging between them; dim doubles per stage while the resolution halves
window: 7x7 windows, with cyclic shift on alternating blocks and a -100 additive attention mask for the shifted ones

window.left: window_size[1] - 1 in each window, split along the height and width axes
window.right: window_size[1] - 1 in each window, split along the height and width axes

fully_masked_row.note: Cannot occur: the image is partitioned into non-overlapping windows and every token of a window attends to every other token of the same window, so no row is empty.

attention.bias: a learned relative-position bias table, indexed by the (h, w) offset inside the window
attention.scale_note: the score is multiplied by a learned logit scale rather than by 1/sqrt(D); it is initialised so that the product starts near ten, which is what makes its value a fact about the weights rather than about the shape

bias: a continuous relative position bias produced by a small MLP over the relative coordinate table, then 16*sigmoid
image_size: pinned at 224. The reference builds its inputs from the module-level image_size but constructs Model() with no arguments, so the constructor's own default of 224 is what the model is built at; the two agree at 224 and at nothing else. Only window_size 7 divides every stage resolution anyway, since they are 56, 28, 14 and 7, so 224 is the usable image for this reference and a case cannot move it.

abi.note: runner is a ModelNew module evaluated in the same process as the reference
